tasks.goal: Fix the independently observed flake in tests/deadline-extension.test.ts test `collect waits for an in-flight grant checkpoint past child exit`, recorded in design/deadline-inflight-stability-v1.md. The focused test passes alone, but full npm test under normal local load failed once because a fixed 2,000ms wait for callbackStarted elapsed before the child/event-loop callback became observable. Diagnose whether this is fixture timing or a production deadline-state race. Make the test deterministic by synchronizing on an explicit extension callback signal or repeated marker with a separately generous diagnostic deadline rather than racing startup against a fixed short assertion window. Preserve the exact semantics: collect must remain pending after child exit while grant persistence is unresolved; the callback must observe cumulativeTimeoutMs 2600; after release, the same single extension permits a successful result. Keep the existing late-result timeout regression and all other deadline tests. If, and only if, a deterministic reproduction proves src/agents/claude.ts has a real race, make the narrowest production fix and explain it in code comments. Do not skip, delete, mark todo, or weaken the test. Run build, the full deadline-extension file repeatedly enough to demonstrate stability, and the complete test suite.
nonGoals: Do not remove or skip the flaky test.
Do not add arbitrary long sleeps as the primary synchronization.
Do not change adoption, journal, routing or queue semantics.
deliverables: The in-flight grant test synchronizes without a startup race.
The production deadline and persistence semantics remain unchanged unless a proven race is fixed.
The focused file and full suite pass independently.
forbidden: Do not mark the test skipped or todo.
Do not change files outside writePaths.
Do not suppress a real bind or process failure.
